s3_subtitle: From a humble Stuttgart workshop to global industry leader for piano actions and hammerheads
s3_notes: Slide 3: Timeline of 140+ years of tradition (9 milestones). Key focus on Milestone 1 (1882: Founding in Stuttgart – The journey begins with piano actions; parallel to Carl Rönisch), Milestone 2 (1906: Dedicated hammerhead manufacturing – From Cristofori's leather-covered paper roll in 1700 to Renner's proprietary hammerhead production from 1906, which would later define the tone of every Steinway grand and establish a worldwide benchmark; image series featuring Cristofori, 1700 hammer action, historical action manufacturing and 1906 hammerhead presses), Milestone 3 (1911: Modernization & grand action manufacturing – Érard repetition action as cornerstone of modern grand piano playing; transition to Renner's first grand piano actions; Oscar Renner's industrial modernization with cutting-edge machinery, streamlined methods and transition from shaft drives to hundreds of individual electric motors; uniting all branches under one roof; image series featuring Sébastien Érard, 1808 Érard action and electrified workshop), Milestone 4 (1944: Air raid & rebuilding), Milestone 5 (1951/1952: Dr. Manfred Renner; 1955 return), Milestone 6 (1990: Fall of the Wall, historic turning point & survival – acquisition of Piano Union's action facility in Zeitz amidst pressure from Czech competitors to preserve largest customer Schimmel producing >40 pianos/day), Milestone 7 (2011: New facility in Gärtringen and modern manufacturing in Meuselwitz after relocating from Zeitz; consolidation across two core sites: Meuselwitz 6,800 m² and Gärtringen; image series featuring Gärtringen new facility and Meuselwitz bird's-eye view), Milestone 8 (2019: Steinway & Sons acquisition; tribute to Clemens von Arnim) and Milestone 9 (Preserving tradition, shaping future: Full consolidation of all operations in Meuselwitz following October 2025 launch with modern facility and new central filtration & extraction system; gratitude to Gärtringen workforce).

Introduce the 6 historical milestones: 1783 founding in Wurzen by J.D. Weickert, 1847 invention of Germany's first viable piano felt (replacing leather hammer covers), 1850-1867 London & Paris World Expos with royal honors, 1861 industrial expansion at Wurzen Mühlgraben with steam engines and soft Mulde water, 1906 world leader for 200,000 pianos annually (Steinway New York), and today the renaissance of 'Weickert Spezial' exclusively for Louis Renner. s6_title: Pure Virgin Wool: Preserving Natural Fiber Elasticity
s6_subtitle: Only uncompressed raw wool guarantees maximum natural elasticity
s6_bullet_1: Bale Delivery Without Over-Compression: Raw wool is transported in loosely packed bales. Excessive compression would irreversibly damage the delicate scales and crimp of the wool fibers.
s6_bullet_2: Higher Logistics Costs for Supreme Quality: This gentle handling increases transport volume, but safeguards intact fiber elasticity.
s6_bullet_3: Pronounced Fiber Crimp: Only highly crimped Merino wool fibers provide optimal interlocking during the subsequent fulling process.
s6_bullet_4: Gentle Carbonization: A chemically gentle cleansing process removes plant matter without attacking the keratin protein structure.

s8_title: Carding: Parallel Alignment into Flowing Fleece
s8_subtitle: Defined fiber orientation as the foundation for resonance and string response
s8_bullet_1: Carding: Loosened fibers are combed through fine wire rollers, untangled, and arranged in parallel alignment.
s8_bullet_2: Defined Fiber Direction: The resulting gossamer-thin, soft web features a precisely specified preferential fiber orientation.
s8_bullet_3: Layering: Multiple web layers are superimposed in cross-lap and longitudinal arrangements to build the required sheet thickness and density gradient.
s8_bullet_4: Prerequisite for Voicing: Only parallel-aligned fibers react predictably and evenly to voicing needle penetration during subsequent tone regulation.

s40_title: Calculating Boring Length without Existing Samples
s40_subtitle: The proven 4-step calculation method developed by Renner Academy
s40_caption_1: Measurement diagram for determining hammer boring depth in grands
s40_bullet_1: 1. Blow Distance & Key Dip: Measure action blow distance (46–48 mm) and key dip (10–10.5 mm) precisely.
s40_bullet_2: 2. Flange Rail Reference: Use height of flange rail relative to string underside as datum plane.
s40_bullet_3: 3. Apply Rule of Thumb: Boring length = overall length - 24 mm for standard grand piano geometries.
s40_bullet_4: 4. Mathematical Verification: Ensure a shank protrusion of at least 3 mm for structural integrity.

s47_title: The Taper Principle: Conical Shank & Conical Hole
s47_subtitle: Why cylindrical bores fail and conical friction locking creates indestructible joints
s47_bullet_1: No Glue Scraping: With cylindrical shanks, sliding the head on pushes glue outward – starving the joint of adhesive.
s47_bullet_2: Even Glue Film: With conical fits, wood surfaces make contact only across the final fraction of a millimeter.
s47_bullet_3: Wood Swelling Creates Wedge Lock: Moisture in the glue swells wood fibers in the bore, locking the shank in an unbreakable friction weld.
